newsitem.title: LEBANON: ESCWA region 1997 GDP growth seen slower.
newsitem.headline: ESCWA region 1997 GDP growth seen slower.

text.p: Economic growth among the 13 members of the U.N.'s Economic and Social Commission for Western Asia will slow to 3.7 percent in 1997 from 4.3 percent in 1996, an ESCWA report said.
It called the projected growth "fairly positive" despite the slowdown.

The preliminary report, distributed at ESCWA's bi-annual ministerial meeting which opened in Beirut on Wednesday, covered Bahrain, Egypt, Iraq, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Oman, Palestinian self-rule areas, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Syria, the United Arab Emirates and Yemen.

Syria led the region with 5.9 percent growth in 1996, followed by Kuwait 5.7 percent, Oman and Jordan 5.2 percent, Egypt 4.9 percent, Yemen 4.8 percent, Lebanon four percent and an average 4.1 percent for Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries, the report said.
It did not give rates for Iraq or the Palestinian self-rule areas.
The economic outlook for ESCWA countries would be affected by an expected decline in international oil prices, the pace of economic reforms and peace developments, the report said.
"Positive developments (in the peace process) would encourage foreign and domestic investment and increase revenues from tourism," it said.
Israel's peace talks with the Palestinians and with Syria and Lebanon are currently stalled.
The report said oil prices were expected to fall below 1996's $20 per barrel.
"This will significantly affect the GCC countries. It would reduce their balance of trade surpluses, widen their budget deficits and reduce the growth of the non-oil sectors," it said.

The report said many ESCWA countries continued economic reforms in 1996, applying prudent monetary and fiscal policies, reducing import tariffs, introducing new investment laws and increasing the pace of privatisation.
It expected privatisation to accelerate in Kuwait, Egypt and Oman.
It said Bahrain, Egypt, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates reduced their budget deficit ratios to GDP to less than 1.5 percent in 1996, according to preliminary estimates.
Estimated ratios for ESCWA countries excluding Iraq, Syria and the Palestinian areas ranged between 0.2 percent for the UAE and 4.6 percent for Jordan. Lebanon was an estimated 14 percent.
But despite adequate economic growth rates in 1996, unemployment remained a regional problem.
The highest rate was 28 percent in the West Bank and Gaza caused by high population growth and Israel's border closures. It was 25 percent in Yemen and 13 percent in Egypt and Jordan.
However, inflation in ESCWA countries stood at "internationally acceptable levels" in 1996 and was not expected to change much in 1997.

According to preliminary estimates, the highest inflation rate among the ESCWA members, excluding Iraq, was Yemen at 25 percent followed by Syria with 20 percent. Lebanon reported 9.8 percent, Egypt an estimated 7.1 percent and Jordan six percent.
